assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase from last year's level, driven by a sharp rise in reported cases this fall.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 853% increase from last year's level, indicating a significant surge in reported cases this fall.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with an 87% increase from last year's level, though the number of cases has decreased from the previous year.
Global flu test positivity is peaking with a 26% increase from the previous month, and US flu hospital admissions are rising sharply.
Polio Wikipedia readership is at the 98th percentile of the past year, indicating heightened public interest but no reported cases.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1388% increase from last year's level, indicating a sharp rise in reported cases this fall.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 45% increase from last year's level, though the number of cases has decreased from the previous year.
RSV test positivity is rising with a 62% increase from the previous month, and US hospital admissions are increasing sharply.

Chikungunya cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 58/100, showing a slight increase in weekly reports but stable overall. The first locally acquired cases were reported in Switzerland in October 2026.
US COVID-19 hospital admissions are at baseline with a score of 56/100, showing a 13% increase from the previous month. Wikipedia readership is at the 17th percentile of the past year.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a score of 56/100, up 55% from the previous 8 months. This year's cases are significantly lower than last year's.
Malaria cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 50/100, showing a 30% increase in weekly reports but a decrease in annual cases compared to last year.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are at baseline with a score of 50/100, showing a 10% increase in weekly reports but a decrease in annual cases compared to last year.
Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) readership is at the 36th percentile of the past year, indicating a rising trend in public interest.
Typhoid fever readership is at the 42nd percentile of the past year, indicating stable public interest.
